metadata.title: Product Streams
metadata.description: Outcome-based product streams for the Freelancer Bookkeeping Service Platform domain: the client lifecycle from intro call to active client and from a previous bookkeeper to Kees; the everyday administration of receipts, invoices, bank transactions and the dashboard; the filing lifecycle Review -> File VAT -> Close the year -> File income tax, extended to VOFs, BVs (Founders) and payroll; advice from a personal bookkeeper; and the growth and operations journeys (subscription billing, partners and referrals, bookkeeper capacity and quality) that keep a fixed-fee bookkeeping service for 10,000+ entrepreneurs running.
metadata.flowModelNote: Each stream carries only stream-specific flows, names the supporting bricks used in each step and the persona acting in it, and lists the external systems (Ponto and the client's bank, the Belastingdienst digital filing channels, KVK, e-mail, Google Meet, payment providers, the app stores, partner organisations and regulatory sources) the flow depends on.

rootGroups.name: Client Lifecycle Journeys
rootGroups.description: From a website request to an active client with a personal bookkeeper, from a previous bookkeeper or self-service package to a continued administration without gaps, and from plan choice to monthly invoicing, plan changes and cancellation: the journeys that win, switch and keep clients on the fixed-fee model.

streams.name: Start and Onboard a New Client
streams.description: Take a freelancer from a request on keesdeboekhouder.nl to an active client with a personal bookkeeper: a free introduction call via Google Meet, a mutual-fit check (no external accounting software, a legal form Kees serves), the plan for that legal form (eenmanszaak €840, VOF €1,140 for two partners plus €100 per extra partner, holding BV €1,750 or werkmaatschappij €2,450 per year ex VAT, invoiced monthly), account access to the web and mobile app, assignment of an internally trained bookkeeper with a backup colleague, and coaching through the first receipt upload. The six-step onboarding on the website is the promise: request, fit check, account access and bookkeeper, upload receipts, bookkeeper reviews and files, ongoing support.
outcomes: A freelancer who requests an intro call is an active client with a bookkeeper and a first upload within days, not weeks
Every new client is on the right plan for their legal form and knows the first-full-fiscal-year commitment and the monthly invoicing before they sign
Bookkeeper matching balances portfolios across Amsterdam, Rotterdam and Utrecht so the personal relationship starts on day one

flows.title: From Intro Call to Active Client
flows.description: The website request, the free Google Meet introduction, the mutual-fit check, the plan choice, account creation, bookkeeper assignment and the first upload, as run by client success for a new sole proprietor.
flows.trigger: A freelancer books a free introduction call on the website, arrives through a partner benefit link, or asks to be called back.
flows.successSignal: The client has logged in on web and mobile, uploaded a first receipt, received the welcome message from the assigned bookkeeper and the first monthly invoice is scheduled.

steps.title: Capture the request and book the free intro call
keyFacts: The website offers a free introduction via Google Meet; the request records name, legal form (or intention to register at KVK), sector and how the freelancer heard about Kees, including any partner referral code.
Intro calls are scheduled in the client success calendar within a few working days, and a confirmation with the meeting link goes out by e-mail.
painPoints: Freelancers who fill in the form late in the evening and hear nothing for days book a trial with a software-only competitor in the meantime.
Requests without a legal form or KVK status cannot be routed to the right package before the call.

dependencies.name: Lead Capture and Intro Call Booking
dependencies.how: Captures the request, referral source and preferred slot and books the Google Meet introduction.

dependencies.name: Client Messaging, E-mail and Call Log
dependencies.how: Sends the confirmation and a reminder before the intro call.

steps.title: Run the intro call and check mutual fit
keyFacts: The executive explains the fixed-fee model, that the app replaces external accounting software (external packages are not accepted) and that a first full fiscal year is the commitment; the freelancer explains their business and current administration.

The fit check records legal form, expected revenue, VAT status (including a possible KOR choice under €20,000 turnover), whether a bank connection is wanted and whether the freelancer is switching from a previous bookkeeper.
painPoints: Freelancers who expect to keep using another accounting package are disappointed late in the call instead of seeing the boundary on the website.
Calls that drift into tax advice before the client is active create expectations the bookkeeper later has to correct.

dependencies.name: Onboarding, Fit Check and Bookkeeper Matching
dependencies.how: Records the fit-check answers and the decision to proceed, decline or refer to Founders for a BV.

dependencies.name: Lead Capture and Intro Call Booking
dependencies.how: Marks the lead as qualified, declined or nurturing.

steps.title: Choose the plan for the legal form and confirm the terms
keyFacts: The plan follows the legal form: eenmanszaak €840, VOF €1,140 for two partners plus €100 per extra partner, holding BV €1,750 and werkmaatschappij €2,450 per year ex VAT through Founders; add-ons are the bank connection at €5 per month per account, the partner income tax return at €125 incl. VAT and payroll at €17.50 per payslip.
The first year covers the full fiscal year; afterwards the client can cancel monthly with one calendar month notice, and the fee is invoiced monthly.
painPoints: Starters who register at KVK halfway through the year are unsure whether the fiscal-year commitment means twelve months or the remainder of the calendar year.
VOFs that add a partner later are surprised by the extra €100 per partner if it was not written down at signing.

dependencies.name: Subscription Plans, Billing and Cancellation
dependencies.how: Creates the subscription with plan, add-ons, start date, fiscal-year commitment and monthly invoicing.

dependencies.name: Onboarding, Fit Check and Bookkeeper Matching
dependencies.how: Records the accepted plan and terms in the onboarding case.

steps.title: Create the client account and give access to web and mobile
keyFacts: The client account is created with the KVK number, legal form, trading names and VAT number; the freelancer receives login access to mijn.keesdeboekhouder.nl and the iOS or Android app.
Starters who are not yet registered at KVK get the account prepared and finish the KVK and VAT number details after registration.
painPoints: A wrong legal form at account creation propagates into VAT setup, the dashboard and the year-end deductions.
Clients who never install the mobile app upload receipts in batches at quarter end instead of as they go.

dependencies.name: Identity, Login and Access Control
dependencies.how: Creates the user identity, sends the activation e-mail and enforces access to the client's own administration only.

dependencies.name: Mobile App Shell (iOS/Android)
dependencies.how: Lets the client log in on iOS or Android and enables push notifications.

dependencies.name: Onboarding, Fit Check and Bookkeeper Matching
dependencies.how: Stores KVK number, legal form, trading names and VAT number on the onboarding case.

steps.title: Assign the personal bookkeeper and a backup colleague
keyFacts: The client is matched to an internally trained bookkeeper based on office (Amsterdam, Rotterdam or Utrecht), sector experience (creative professionals, consultants, starters), language and current portfolio size, with a colleague as backup.
The bookkeeper introduces themselves with a welcome message and explains how to reach them by e-mail and phone, with a video or in-person meeting on request.
painPoints: Assigning by availability alone puts a photographer with a bookkeeper who has never seen a DuPho member's cost structure.
Bookkeepers with full portfolios receive new clients when there is no live view of capacity per office.

dependencies.name: Client Allocation and Workload Planning
dependencies.how: Proposes bookkeepers with capacity in the right office and sector and records the assignment and backup.

dependencies.name: Onboarding, Fit Check and Bookkeeper Matching
dependencies.how: Confirms the match and moves the case to active.

dependencies.name: Client Messaging, E-mail and Call Log
dependencies.how: Sends the bookkeeper's welcome message and contact details.

steps.title: Coach the client through the first receipts and invoices
keyFacts: The bookkeeper asks for the first receipts and purchase invoices via Scan & Herken and, if the client is mid-year, the opening balances and any invoices already sent; a first to-do list appears on the dashboard.
The first submitted bookings are checked quickly so the client learns what a good upload looks like and which private costs stay out.
painPoints: Clients who get no feedback on the first upload keep photographing receipts wrongly (cut-off VAT, no supplier) for a whole quarter.
A shoebox of paper receipts from earlier in the year turns the first review into days of work.

dependencies.name: Scan & Herken Receipt Capture and Recognition
dependencies.how: Recognises the first photographed receipts and shows the client the recognised supplier, amount and VAT.

dependencies.name: Deadlines, To-dos and Notifications
dependencies.how: Lists the first to-dos (upload receipts, add invoices, connect the bank) on the dashboard and app.

dependencies.name: Client Messaging, E-mail and Call Log
dependencies.how: Carries the bookkeeper's feedback on the first uploads.

flows.title: Onboard a Starter Who Is Registering at KVK
flows.description: A starting entrepreneur, often next to a job, is guided from KVK registration to a correctly set-up administration: VAT number, a possible KOR choice, startersaftrek and hours criterion, first invoice and first quarter.
flows.trigger: A starter books an intro call before or just after registering at KVK, often through a starter blog post, a partner or a friend who is a Kees client.
flows.successSignal: The starter has a KVK number, VAT number and correct VAT status in the account, knows the hours criterion and startersaftrek rules and sends the first invoice from the app.

steps.title: Explain the Starters package and the first-year terms
keyFacts: The Starters package is the same €840 per year eenmanszaak subscription with starter guidance on KVK, the VAT number, the KOR, startersaftrek and the hours criterion.
The intro call clarifies that the first full fiscal year is the commitment and that the fee is invoiced monthly, so a part-time starter can see the cost against expected revenue.
painPoints: Starters next to a job doubt whether €70 per month is worth it before the first revenue arrives.
The choice between the KOR and normal VAT is made too late, after the first invoice without VAT has gone out.

dependencies.name: Lead Capture and Intro Call Booking
dependencies.how: Captures the starter's intention and KVK status.

dependencies.name: Onboarding, Fit Check and Bookkeeper Matching
dependencies.how: Records the starter-specific questions (KVK date, job next to business, expected turnover).

steps.title: Register at KVK and obtain the VAT number
keyFacts: The starter registers the eenmanszaak at KVK; the Belastingdienst then issues a VAT identification number and a turnover tax number, which are entered into the account.
The starter decides with guidance whether to apply for the KOR (VAT exemption up to €20,000 turnover, relaxed since 1 January 2025) or to charge VAT and reclaim input VAT.
painPoints: Invoices sent before the VAT number arrives have to be corrected or credited later.
Starters who apply for the KOR without understanding that they cannot reclaim VAT on a laptop or camera regret it at year end.

dependencies.name: Onboarding, Fit Check and Bookkeeper Matching
dependencies.how: Captures the KVK number, VAT numbers and KOR decision on the onboarding case.

dependencies.name: Advice Knowledge Base and Tax Rules Content
dependencies.how: Provides the starter article on the KOR threshold and VAT registration used in the guidance.

steps.title: Set up the account with the right VAT status and trading name
keyFacts: The account is configured with legal form eenmanszaak, VAT status (normal or KOR), the trading name(s) and the start date, which drives the quarterly VAT cycle and the year-end deductions.
Multiple trading names per entity are supported, so a designer who also sells prints uses one administration.
painPoints: A KOR client set up as a normal VAT client receives VAT-return to-dos they do not need.
Trading names added later without telling the bookkeeper appear on invoices the bookkeeper cannot place.

dependencies.name: Identity, Login and Access Control
dependencies.how: Activates the login and links it to the new administration.

dependencies.name: Subscription Plans, Billing and Cancellation
dependencies.how: Starts the €840 per year subscription with the monthly invoice schedule.

dependencies.name: Onboarding, Fit Check and Bookkeeper Matching
dependencies.how: Passes VAT status and trading names to the administration setup.

steps.title: Match with a bookkeeper experienced with starters
keyFacts: Starters are matched with bookkeepers who regularly handle first VAT returns, startersaftrek and the hours criterion questions, in the office nearest to the starter.
The backup colleague is named in the welcome message so a holiday never blocks a first question.
painPoints: Starter questions (can I deduct my home office, my phone, my course) are the most frequent and the most time-consuming for a bookkeeper who is not prepared for them.
A starter who does not get a fast first answer stops uploading and returns at quarter end with a backlog.

dependencies.name: Client Allocation and Workload Planning
dependencies.how: Assigns a bookkeeper with starter experience and capacity.

dependencies.name: Client Messaging, E-mail and Call Log
dependencies.how: Sends the welcome message with e-mail and phone contact.

steps.title: Walk through the app, the first invoice and the first receipts
keyFacts: The bookkeeper walks the starter through the mobile app: photograph a receipt with Scan & Herken, send a first invoice with the right VAT rate, and read the dashboard's VAT to pay per quarter.
Push and e-mail notifications remind the starter of the upcoming VAT return and of receipts still to upload.
painPoints: Starters who never open the app before the first quarter deadline learn the VAT return the hard way.
Investments bought before the KVK registration are often forgotten as deductible start-up costs.

dependencies.name: Mobile App Shell (iOS/Android)
dependencies.how: Provides the app the starter uses for the first receipts and invoice.

dependencies.name: Scan & Herken Receipt Capture and Recognition
dependencies.how: Recognises the first uploads and flags missing supplier or VAT data.

dependencies.name: Deadlines, To-dos and Notifications
dependencies.how: Schedules reminders for the first VAT return and outstanding to-dos.

steps.title: Record hours criterion and startersaftrek expectations
keyFacts: The bookkeeper explains the hours criterion (1,225 hours a year) that gates zelfstandigenaftrek (€1,200 in 2026) and startersaftrek (€2,123), and asks the starter to keep an hours log from day one.
The expectation is noted on the client file so the year-end close checks the log before applying the deductions.
painPoints: Part-time starters next to a job rarely meet the hours criterion and are disappointed when the deductions do not apply.
Hours logs reconstructed in March for the previous year are weak evidence in a Belastingdienst check.

dependencies.name: Advice Knowledge Base and Tax Rules Content
dependencies.how: Provides the current zelfstandigenaftrek, startersaftrek and hours criterion content.

dependencies.name: Client Messaging, E-mail and Call Log
dependencies.how: Records the advice given and the starter's confirmation on the client file.

streams.name: Switch from a Previous Bookkeeper
streams.description: Move an existing freelancer or VOF from another bookkeeper, accountant or self-service package to Kees without a gap in the VAT or income tax history: collect digital copies of old returns and annual accounts, personal and entity data, the current-year bookings and opening balances, agree who files the return in progress, and give the new bookkeeper a complete file from the first quarter onwards. The switch service is run by client success with the bookkeeper and is a common route by which established freelancers join.
outcomes: A switching client's VAT and income tax history is continuous: no missed quarter, no double filing, no unknown opening balance
Historical returns and annual accounts are stored digitally in the client file so the bookkeeper never has to ask for them again
The previous bookkeeper's ledgers are converted into Kees bookings within the first quarter so the dashboard is accurate from the switch date

flows.title: Switch an Established Freelancer Mid-year
flows.description: A knowledge freelancer leaves an hourly-billed accountant halfway through the year: the switch service collects the history, imports the current year, agrees the filing hand-over and activates the new bookkeeper.
flows.trigger: A freelancer with an existing administration decides during the intro call to switch to Kees from a certain quarter.
flows.successSignal: The current-year bookings and opening balances are in the Kees administration, the previous returns are archived, the hand-over quarter is filed by exactly one party and the bookkeeper has confirmed the file complete.

steps.title: Agree the switch date and who files the return in progress
keyFacts: The switch date is aligned with a quarter boundary where possible; the fit check records which VAT quarter and which income tax year the previous bookkeeper still files.
The subscription starts on the switch date and the first full fiscal year commitment is explained together with the monthly invoice.
painPoints: Switching on the 15th of the last month of a quarter leaves nobody clearly responsible for that quarter's VAT return.
Previous bookkeepers who are still owed money delay the hand-over of data.

dependencies.name: Onboarding, Fit Check and Bookkeeper Matching
dependencies.how: Records the previous bookkeeper, the switch date and the filing responsibilities per return.

dependencies.name: Subscription Plans, Billing and Cancellation
dependencies.how: Starts the plan on the switch date.

dependencies.name: Filing Calendar and Deadline Orchestration
dependencies.how: Registers which upcoming deadlines Kees owns from the switch date.

steps.title: Collect digital copies of old returns, annual accounts and entity data
keyFacts: The client uploads digital copies of the last income tax returns, VAT returns, annual accounts and the KVK extract; personal data (BSN, address, partner) needed for the income tax return is collected AVG-compliantly.
A checklist per legal form shows what is still missing and the client is reminded until the file is complete.
painPoints: Returns are often only available as a PDF from the previous accountant's portal that closes when the engagement ends.
Personal data sent as loose e-mail attachments creates an AVG risk and an incomplete file.

dependencies.name: Switch Service and Historical Data Import
dependencies.how: Lists required historical documents per legal form and tracks completeness.

dependencies.name: Document Archive
dependencies.how: Stores the old returns and annual accounts in the client's document archive.

dependencies.name: Identity, Login and Access Control
dependencies.how: Gives the client an authenticated upload channel instead of e-mail attachments.

steps.title: Import the current-year bookings and opening balances
keyFacts: The previous bookkeeper's ledger export (or the client's spreadsheet) is imported and mapped to the Kees booking rules; opening balances for bank, receivables, payables and investments are set on the switch date.
Investments in progress (a camera, a laptop, a car) carry their depreciation schedule over so the year-end is correct.
painPoints: Exports from self-service packages use different VAT codes and cost categories, so unmapped lines end up as 'other costs'.
A missing opening bank balance makes the first bank reconciliation impossible.

dependencies.name: Switch Service and Historical Data Import
dependencies.how: Imports and maps the historical ledger and opening balances.

dependencies.name: General Ledger and Booking Rules
dependencies.how: Posts the opening balances and the imported bookings under Kees booking rules.

steps.title: Reconcile the hand-over quarter with the previous filings
keyFacts: The bookkeeper reconciles the imported bookings with the last VAT return filed by the previous bookkeeper so that the first Kees VAT return starts from a matching position.
Differences are booked as corrections in the first Kees quarter or flagged to the client for a supplementary return.
painPoints: A previous bookkeeper who filed on estimates leaves a difference that surfaces only in the annual accounts.
Clients do not know whether the previous bookkeeper already claimed the VAT on a large investment.

dependencies.name: VAT Return Preparation
dependencies.how: Compares the imported ledger with the previously filed VAT positions.

dependencies.name: Bookkeeper Client File and Review Queue
dependencies.how: Puts the reconciliation on the bookkeeper's review queue.

steps.title: Confirm the file complete and inform the client
keyFacts: The bookkeeper confirms the switch file complete, the client receives a summary of what was taken over and what Kees files from now on, and the dashboard shows the current year from the switch date.
The previous bookkeeper is informed of the switch by the client, with Kees providing a standard message when asked.
painPoints: Without a written confirmation the client keeps sending questions to both bookkeepers.
A dashboard that starts at zero on the switch date confuses clients who expect the year to date.

dependencies.name: Client Messaging, E-mail and Call Log
dependencies.how: Sends the summary of the completed switch and the filing responsibilities.

dependencies.name: Switch Service and Historical Data Import
dependencies.how: Closes the switch case with the completeness confirmation.

flows.title: Switch a VOF from a Self-service Package
flows.description: Two partners who kept their own books in a self-service package move to Kees: the shared administration is rebuilt, the profit split and each partner's history are imported and both partners get access.
flows.trigger: A VOF that outgrew self-service bookkeeping (payroll, a second partner, a first Belastingdienst question) signs up for the VOF package.
flows.successSignal: Both partners have their own login, the shared administration shows the imported year with the agreed profit split, and each partner's previous income tax return is archived.

steps.title: Record the partners and the profit split
keyFacts: The VOF package covers two partners at €1,140 per year with €100 per extra partner; the partnership contract or an agreed percentage defines the profit split used at year end.
Each partner's personal data is collected separately for the individual income tax returns.
painPoints: VOFs without a written partnership contract discover the profit split question at the first year end.
Partners who share one login lose track of who submitted which receipt.

dependencies.name: Onboarding, Fit Check and Bookkeeper Matching
dependencies.how: Records the partners, their shares and the package.

dependencies.name: Subscription Plans, Billing and Cancellation
dependencies.how: Creates the subscription with the number of partners.

dependencies.name: Identity, Login and Access Control
dependencies.how: Creates a login per partner with access to the shared administration.

steps.title: Export and upload the self-service history
keyFacts: The partners export invoices, expenses and bank transactions from the self-service package and upload them together with the filed VAT returns and last year's annual figures.
External accounting software is not used going forward; the export is the last act in the old package.
painPoints: Self-service exports lack receipts as documents, so the Kees archive starts without evidence for older bookings.
Partners export at different times and the two exports overlap or leave a gap.

dependencies.name: Switch Service and Historical Data Import
dependencies.how: Guides the export and upload of the self-service history.

dependencies.name: Document Archive
dependencies.how: Stores the filed returns and annual figures.

steps.title: Rebuild the shared administration with opening balances
keyFacts: The imported history is mapped to Kees booking rules, opening balances are posted per partner capital account and the VAT position at the switch date is set.
Trading names and the shared bank account are linked to the one administration both partners see.
painPoints: Private withdrawals booked as costs in the self-service package distort the partners' capital accounts.
Two bank accounts with mixed private and business use take days to untangle.

dependencies.name: Switch Service and Historical Data Import
dependencies.how: Maps the history to Kees categories.

dependencies.name: General Ledger and Booking Rules
dependencies.how: Posts opening balances per partner and the VAT position.

steps.title: Review and reconcile with the last filed VAT return
keyFacts: The bookkeeper checks the rebuilt quarter against the last VAT return the partners filed themselves and lists corrections.
A four-eyes check is standard for switches because the history was not produced by a Kees bookkeeper.
painPoints: Self-filed returns often used the wrong VAT rate on mixed deliveries, and corrections need a supplementary return.
Partners disagree about who submitted what, so the reconciliation becomes a mediation.

dependencies.name: VAT Return Preparation
dependencies.how: Compares the rebuilt ledger with the self-filed VAT return.

dependencies.name: Bookkeeper Client File and Review Queue
dependencies.how: Schedules the review and the corrections on the queue.

steps.title: Hand over to the personal bookkeeper and set the first deadlines
keyFacts: The assigned bookkeeper receives the completed switch file, both partners get the welcome message and the filing calendar shows the first Kees VAT return for the VOF and the two partner income tax returns.
The partners are told how the profit split appears on the dashboard and in each partner's return.
painPoints: Switch files handed over without a note about open corrections cause the bookkeeper to redo the reconciliation.
Partners expect two dashboards and are confused by one shared view.

dependencies.name: Filing Calendar and Deadline Orchestration
dependencies.how: Registers the VOF's VAT deadline and both partners' income tax return in the calendar.

dependencies.name: Client Messaging, E-mail and Call Log
dependencies.how: Sends the welcome and the switch summary to both partners.

dependencies.name: Bookkeeper Client File and Review Queue
dependencies.how: Transfers the completed switch file to the bookkeeper's client file.

streams.name: Manage Subscription Billing and Plans
streams.description: Run the fixed-fee subscription from plan choice to monthly invoicing and collection, add-ons (bank connection €5 per month per connected account, partner income tax return €125 incl. VAT, payroll €17.50 per payslip per employee per month), plan changes when the legal form changes (extra VOF partner at €100, eenmanszaak to BV via Founders), the first-full-fiscal-year commitment and monthly cancellation with one calendar month notice afterwards. The stream keeps the transparent price promise that distinguishes Kees from hourly-billed accountants.
outcomes: Every client is invoiced the right monthly amount for their plan and add-ons with no surprise bills, ever
Plan changes (extra partner, bank account, payroll, BV) take effect on the right date and are visible to the client and the bookkeeper
Cancellations follow the first-fiscal-year and one-calendar-month rules consistently and are logged for retention analysis

flows.title: Invoice the Fixed Fee Monthly with Add-ons
flows.description: The monthly billing run: plan fee per legal form, add-ons counted from usage (connected bank accounts, payslips, partner returns), invoice, collection and dunning for the subscription itself.
flows.trigger: The monthly billing date arrives for all active subscriptions, or a client activates an add-on during the month.
flows.successSignal: All active clients received a correct monthly invoice, add-ons match actual usage, payments are collected and failed collections are followed up.

steps.title: Determine the monthly fee per plan and legal form
keyFacts: The yearly fee (eenmanszaak €840, VOF €1,140 for two partners plus €100 per extra partner, holding BV €1,750, werkmaatschappij €2,450, all ex VAT) is invoiced monthly; the starters package uses the eenmanszaak fee.
Plan and legal form are read from the subscription, and a mid-month start is prorated by the rules agreed at onboarding.
painPoints: A legal form changed in the administration but not in the subscription produces the wrong fee for months.
Prorating rules that differ between sales conversations create disputes on the first invoice.

dependencies.name: Subscription Plans, Billing and Cancellation
dependencies.how: Derives the monthly amount from plan, legal form and partner count.

dependencies.name: Onboarding, Fit Check and Bookkeeper Matching
dependencies.how: Provides the start date and prorating agreed at onboarding.

steps.title: Count add-ons from actual usage
keyFacts: Connected bank accounts (€5 per month each), payslips produced in the month (€17.50 per payslip per employee) and partner income tax returns (€125 incl. VAT, once a year) are counted from the systems that produce them.
Add-ons appear as separate lines on the invoice so the client sees what the fixed fee covers and what is extra.
painPoints: A bank account disconnected mid-month but still counted breaks the transparent-price promise.
Payslip counts entered by hand drift from what payroll actually produced.

dependencies.name: Bank Connection (Ponto PSD2)
dependencies.how: Reports the number of connected bank accounts per client per month.

dependencies.name: Payroll and Payslips
dependencies.how: Reports payslips produced per client per month.

dependencies.name: Income Tax Return (IB) Preparation
dependencies.how: Reports partner income tax returns prepared for the client.

steps.title: Generate and send the monthly subscription invoice
keyFacts: The invoice with plan fee, add-ons and VAT is generated, sent by e-mail and stored in the client's document archive; it is also booked automatically as a cost in the client's own administration.
Clients see the invoice and the payment status in the app.
painPoints: Subscription invoices that are not booked automatically are forgotten as a deductible cost.
Invoices sent to an old e-mail address go unpaid without anyone noticing.

dependencies.name: Subscription Plans, Billing and Cancellation
dependencies.how: Creates and sends the invoice and books it into the client's administration.

dependencies.name: Deadlines, To-dos and Notifications
dependencies.how: Notifies the client that the monthly invoice is available.

steps.title: Collect payment by direct debit or payment link
keyFacts: Payment is collected by SEPA direct debit or an iDEAL payment link through the payment provider; the payment status flows back to the subscription.
Clients with a bank connection see the debit matched automatically against the subscription invoice in their own administration.
painPoints: Failed direct debits at the start of the month cluster around clients with irregular income.
Payment status that arrives with delay makes client success chase clients who have already paid.

dependencies.name: Integration and API Gateway (Ponto, Belastingdienst, KVK, e-mail, payments)

rootGroups.name: Everyday Administration Journeys
rootGroups.description: From a photographed receipt, a sent invoice and a synced bank transaction to a complete administration the client can read on the dashboard: the journeys that make administration take almost no time for the freelancer and leave only exceptions for the bookkeeper.

streams.name: Capture Receipts and Expenses
streams.description: Turn a photographed receipt, an uploaded PDF or a forwarded e-mail into a recognised, categorised expense booking with the right VAT, stored with its document and ready for the bookkeeper's review. Scan & Herken recognises supplier, date, amount and VAT; booking rules propose the cost category and flag private, mixed or investment items; the client confirms in seconds on the phone and the bookkeeper only sees exceptions. This is the stream that makes 'administration takes almost no time' true for creative freelancers with many small receipts.
outcomes: A receipt goes from photo to confirmed booking in under a minute on the phone, so clients capture costs as they go instead of at quarter end
Recognition and booking rules classify the large majority of expenses without bookkeeper touch, leaving only exceptions for review
Every booking carries its document, so the 7-year fiscal retention duty and any Belastingdienst question are covered from the archive

flows.title: Photograph and Book a Receipt on the Phone
flows.description: The everyday path: a designer photographs a receipt in the app, Scan & Herken recognises it, a category and VAT are proposed, the client confirms and the booking with its document lands in the ledger and the review queue.
flows.trigger: The client buys materials, a train ticket, a lunch with a client or a subscription and has the receipt in hand or in the mailbox.
flows.successSignal: The expense is booked with the correct category and VAT, the document is archived, the dashboard cost categories are updated and the bookkeeper sees it only if it was flagged.

steps.title: Photograph the receipt or forward the invoice by e-mail
keyFacts: The app captures a photo (multi-page for longer invoices), accepts PDF uploads, and a personal e-mail-in address forwards supplier invoices straight into the administration.
Receipts can be captured offline and are uploaded when the phone is back online.
painPoints: Thermal receipts fade within months, so photographing later is often too late.
Suppliers who e-mail invoices to a private mailbox are forgotten unless forwarding is a habit.

steps.title: Recognise supplier, amount, date and VAT
keyFacts: Scan & Herken extracts supplier, invoice date, total, VAT amount and rate (21%, 9%, 0% or reverse charge) and shows a confidence per field; low-confidence fields are highlighted for the client.
Recognised suppliers are remembered, so the second receipt from the same shop is proposed with the previous category.
painPoints: Receipts with multiple VAT rates (a supermarket receipt with food and non-food) are the main recognition error.
Foreign invoices without Dutch VAT are recognised as 21% unless the reverse-charge rule is known.

dependencies.name: Scan & Herken Receipt Capture and Recognition

steps.title: Propose the cost category, VAT treatment and private share
keyFacts: Booking rules propose the category (materials, travel, phone and internet, software, representation, investment above the threshold) and apply the rules for limited deductibility of food and drink and for mixed private use.
Investments are flagged so they are depreciated rather than expensed, and the client is asked whether an item is for private use in part.
painPoints: Clients book a €1,500 camera as a cost and are surprised when the bookkeeper moves it to investments.
Representation costs with limited deductibility are the most frequently miscategorised item by starters.

steps.title: Confirm or correct the booking in seconds
keyFacts: The client confirms with one tap or corrects supplier, category or VAT; the booking is posted to the ledger and the document is linked to it.
Corrections train the supplier memory for the next receipt.
painPoints: Clients who confirm everything blindly push errors to the bookkeeper's review.
A correction screen with too many fields makes clients postpone confirmation.

keyFacts: Bookings with low recognition confidence, unusual amounts, possible private items, investments and foreign VAT are flagged on the bookkeeper's queue; the rest is accepted as submitted until the quarterly check.
The bookkeeper can ask the client a question about a specific booking from the queue.
painPoints: A queue that shows every booking hides the ones that need attention.
Questions about a receipt from two months ago are hard for the client to answer.

Seeing the VAT reclaim grow is what motivates clients to keep capturing receipts.
painPoints: Clients who cannot see the effect of a booking do not understand why the bookkeeper wants every receipt.
A dashboard that only updates after review feels stale.

flows.successSignal: All receipts for the quarter are booked and archived before the bookkeeper starts the quarterly check, without a rush on deadline day.

keyFacts: The app and e-mail remind the client that the quarter is closing, listing weeks without bookings and bank transactions without a matching receipt.
Reminders start early in the month after the quarter so the bookkeeper has time to review before the last day of the month.
painPoints: Reminders sent only on deadline day produce a flood of uploads the bookkeeper cannot review in time.
Generic reminders are ignored; reminders that name the missing transactions get a response.

painPoints: Duplicates between a photographed receipt and the same invoice forwarded by e-mail double the costs.
A batch of fifty items with no grouping is abandoned halfway.

Clients skip the unrecognised leftovers and the quarter closes with them unbooked.

streams.name: Create Quotes and Invoices and Get Paid
streams.description: From a quote to an invoice to money in the bank: templates in the client's own style, multiple trading names per entity, VAT rules incl. reverse charge for EU business clients and the KOR exemption, credit notes, status tracking (sent, viewed, paid, overdue), automatic payment reminders and matching against the bank transaction. Every sent invoice is a revenue booking, so the dashboard's revenue per quarter and VAT to pay are always current without the bookkeeper retyping anything.
outcomes: Clients send a professional quote or invoice from the phone in a minute and get paid faster with reminders they do not have to write
Every invoice is a correct revenue and VAT booking the moment it is sent, so revenue per quarter and VAT to pay are never estimates
Reverse charge, KOR and multiple trading names are handled by rules, not by the client's memory

flows.title: From Quote to Invoice to Payment
flows.description: A consultant sends a quote to a new client, converts the accepted quote into an invoice with the right VAT, the invoice is booked as revenue, reminders go out and the payment is matched from the bank.
flows.trigger: A prospective client asks the freelancer for a proposal, or a project milestone is reached and can be invoiced.
flows.successSignal: The invoice is paid and matched, revenue and VAT to pay are updated on the dashboard and the invoice document is archived.

steps.title: Draft the quote in the freelancer's own style and trading name
keyFacts: The quote uses a template with logo, colours and terms, one of the client's trading names, line items with hourly or fixed prices and the VAT rate per line; it can be sent as a PDF by e-mail with a link to accept.
Quotes for creative work often need a deposit line and a validity date.
painPoints: Quotes made in a word processor are not linked to the later invoice, so the bookkeeper cannot see what was agreed.
Clients who use one trading name for design and another for teaching mix them up on documents.

dependencies.name: Quotes and Proposals
dependencies.how: Creates the quote with template, trading name, lines and VAT.

dependencies.name: Mobile App Shell (iOS/Android)
dependencies.how: Lets the client draft and send the quote from the app.

steps.title: Send the quote and track acceptance
keyFacts: The quote is e-mailed with a viewing link; status moves from sent to viewed to accepted or declined, and reminders can be sent before the validity date.
Accepted quotes are the basis for the invoice and for the revenue forecast.
painPoints: Freelancers do not know whether a quote was even opened and wait too long to follow up.
Accepted quotes that are never invoiced are lost revenue nobody notices.

dependencies.name: Quotes and Proposals

steps.title: Convert to an invoice with the right VAT rule
keyFacts: The accepted quote becomes an invoice with a sequential number per trading name; VAT rules apply 21% or 9%, reverse charge for EU business clients with a valid VAT number, 0% outside the EU and no VAT for KOR clients.
The invoice date and payment term set the due date used by the reminders.
painPoints: Reverse-charge invoices without the client's VAT number and the required wording are rejected by the customer's accountant.
Breaking the invoice number sequence is a classic Belastingdienst finding.

dependencies.name: Document Archive
dependencies.how: Stores the invoice PDF.

steps.title: Book revenue and VAT to pay the moment the invoice is sent
keyFacts: Sending the invoice posts revenue and output VAT to the ledger and to the quarter's VAT position; the dashboard's revenue per quarter and VAT to pay update immediately.
Credit notes reverse the booking and keep the numbering intact.
painPoints: Freelancers who invoice outside the app have revenue the bookkeeper only sees in the bank, without VAT detail.
Invoices edited after sending break the link between document and booking.

steps.title: Send payment reminders when the invoice is overdue
keyFacts: Automatic reminders go out at configurable intervals after the due date in the freelancer's tone; the client can pause reminders for a customer with an agreed delay.
A payment link on the invoice lets customers pay by iDEAL.
painPoints: Freelancers hate chasing money and delay it, so reminders that go out by themselves are the value.
A reminder sent to a customer who paid yesterday, before the bank sync ran, is embarrassing.

Paid invoices disappear from the overdue list and reminders stop.
painPoints: Customers who pay without the invoice number force manual matching.
A partial payment that is matched as full hides the outstanding balance.

streams.name: Sync and Match Bank Transactions
streams.description: Connect the client's business bank account through Ponto (Isabel Group, PSD2 licence) to Knab, Rabobank, ABN AMRO, bunq and other Ponto-connected banks, synchronise transactions four times a day, match them automatically against invoices, expense bookings and subscription invoices, let the client match or book the remainder directly from the transaction, and keep the consent alive with re-authorisation every 90 to 180 days. The add-on costs €5 per month per connected account and is what turns 'did I book everything' into a list of unmatched transactions.
outcomes: Bank transactions arrive four times a day and the large majority are matched to bookings automatically, so completeness is a short list, not a search
Re-authorisation every 90 to 180 days is done on time by the client, so no quarter starts with a broken connection
Unmatched transactions become bookings in one tap, giving the bookkeeper a fully reconciled bank account at the quarterly check

flows.successSignal: Transactions from the connected account arrive four times a day, historical transactions are imported from the consent date, the first matches are confirmed and the add-on is on the subscription.

painPoints: Clients connect a mixed private and business account and then have to exclude private transactions one by one.
Unclear pricing per account leads to surprise when a second account is connected.

The consent is valid for 90 to 180 days depending on the bank, after which re-authorisation is needed.

streams.name: Monitor Your Finances on the Dashboard
streams.description: Give every client direct insight on web and mobile: revenue per quarter, cost categories, investments, profit, the VAT to pay or receive per quarter and a tax reservation estimate, updated in real time as bookings are submitted, plus deadlines and to-dos. The dashboard is the client's view of the same ledger the bookkeeper works on, so 'how am I doing' and 'what should I set aside' are answered without a phone call, and the bookkeeper's review status is visible per quarter.
outcomes: Clients know their revenue, profit and VAT to pay for the quarter at any moment without asking their bookkeeper

rootGroups.name: Filing and Advice Journeys
rootGroups.description: From submitted bookings to a checked quarter and a filed VAT return, from a full fiscal year to annual accounts and the income tax return, extended to VOF profit splits, BV corporate tax and KVK filings through Founders and payroll per payslip, plus the personal advice that carries the fiscal responsibility: the journeys where the bookkeeper's work meets the Belastingdienst.

streams.name: Review Administration and File VAT Returns
streams.description: The quarterly heartbeat of the service: the bookkeeper checks the client's submitted bookings, matched bank transactions and invoices, resolves questions, prepares the btw-aangifte (and ICP declaration where needed), runs the four-eyes check on higher-risk files and files the return with the Belastingdienst through the official digital channel before the last day of the month after the quarter. With 10,000+ clients this is a batch of thousands of returns per quarter, orchestrated by the filing calendar and the review queue so every client's return is first-time-right and on time.
outcomes: Every client's quarterly VAT return is filed before the last day of the month after the quarter, with the payment amount communicated in time
Review turnaround per client falls as exceptions, not bookings, drive the bookkeeper's work
Filing first-time-right: supplementary returns and Belastingdienst corrections are rare and traceable to a cause

flows.description: A bookkeeper works a portfolio through the quarter close: the calendar opens the quarter, clients are chased for completeness, each administration is checked, the return is prepared and filed, and the client is told what to pay.
flows.trigger: The quarter ends and the filing calendar opens the VAT cycle with the deadline on the last day of the following month.
flows.successSignal: All clients in the portfolio have a filed VAT return with an acknowledgement from the Belastingdienst, the client knows the amount and payment reference, and the review is logged.

steps.title: Open the quarter and prioritise the portfolio
keyFacts: The filing calendar creates a VAT task per client with the deadline (the last day of the month after the quarter) and prioritises by completeness, risk and history of late clients.
KOR clients and clients with annual returns are excluded from the quarterly batch.
painPoints: Working the portfolio alphabetically leaves the hardest files for the last days.
Tasks created for clients who cancelled or moved office clutter the queue.

Clients who are asked the same thing by two channels stop reading both.

Corrections are booked with a reason so the client learns and the audit trail explains the change.
painPoints: Reviewing every booking line by line makes the bookkeeper the bottleneck for growth.
Corrections without a reason are repeated by the client next quarter.

Anomalies (a large refund, a jump in revenue) are explained before filing.

streams.name: Close the Year and File Income Tax
streams.description: From a full fiscal year of reviewed quarters to the annual accounts and the filed inkomstenbelasting: the bookkeeper collects the year-end items (investments and depreciation, private use, hours log, other income, mortgage and partner data), prepares the annual accounts, applies the deductions (zelfstandigenaftrek €1,200 in 2026, startersaftrek €2,123 for eligible starters, mkb-winstvrijstelling), prepares the income tax return, files it and explains the assessment. A fiscal partner's return can be added for €125 incl. VAT. This is where the promise 'no unexpected tax bill' is kept or broken.
outcomes: Every client's annual accounts and income tax return are filed within the season, and the assessment matches the reservation estimate closely enough that no client is surprised
Every deduction the client is entitled to is applied, with the hours criterion and starter status documented
Year-end lead time per client falls because the quarters were reviewed and the year-end items were collected before the season

flows.title: Prepare Annual Accounts and File the Income Tax Return
flows.description: The year-end for a sole proprietor: collect year-end items, close the ledger, prepare the annual accounts, apply deductions, prepare and check the income tax return, file it and explain the outcome.
flows.trigger: The fourth quarter is filed and the filing calendar opens the year-end and income tax season for all clients of the fiscal year.
flows.successSignal: The annual accounts are in the client's archive, the income tax return is filed with an acknowledgement, the client understands the amount and the assessment is later matched to it.

steps.title: Open the season and request the year-end items
keyFacts: The calendar opens a year-end task per client; the client receives a year-end questionnaire: hours worked, other income and jobs, investments and private use, fiscal partner, home ownership and mortgage, pension premiums, health costs and gifts.
Answers are collected in the app and stored on the client file.
painPoints: Questionnaires sent in March arrive when clients are least responsive; sending in January works better.
Missing partner data blocks the return for weeks.

steps.title: Close the ledger and book depreciation, private use and accruals
keyFacts: The bookkeeper books depreciation on investments, private use corrections (car, phone, home office rules), accruals for invoices around year end and the VAT correction for private use, and closes the ledger for the year.
The reviewed quarters make the close a matter of year-end entries, not a re-review.
painPoints: Investments booked as costs during the year have to be found and moved at year end.
Car and home office rules are the most frequent source of wrong year-end entries.

keyFacts: The balance sheet and profit and loss are generated from the closed ledger with comparatives; the annual accounts are stored in the archive and shown to the client on the dashboard as the final year.
The profit is the basis for the income tax return and for a mortgage application later.
painPoints: Clients asked by a mortgage lender for three years of accounts need them in a standard format.
Accounts produced late block the client's own financial decisions.

steps.title: Apply deductions and prepare the income tax return
keyFacts: The return applies zelfstandigenaftrek (€1,200 in 2026, €900 in 2027) and startersaftrek (€2,123) when the hours criterion is met and the starter conditions hold, then mkb-winstvrijstelling, and adds other income, mortgage interest, partner allocation and the other boxes.
The prepared tax is compared with the reservation estimate shown to the client during the year.
painPoints: Deductions applied without a documented hours log are the first thing a Belastingdienst check removes.
A partner allocation done without the partner's data leaves money on the table.

Approval is recorded with a timestamp on the file.
painPoints: Returns filed without explicit client approval cause disputes when the assessment arrives.
Season peaks make second checks the first thing to be skipped.

The reservation estimate for the new year is recalibrated with the actual outcome.
painPoints: Clients who get a filed return without explanation call when the assessment arrives.
Provisional assessments that were too high or too low are not adjusted without the bookkeeper's advice.

streams.name: Serve Partnerships and Companies
streams.description: Extend the fixed-fee model to VOFs and BVs: for a VOF one shared administration, the profit split per partner and each partner's income tax return; for a BV through the sister company Founders (€1,750 per year for a holding, €2,450 for a werkmaatschappij) the vennootschapsbelasting return, the statutory annual accounts and the KVK filing, DGA salary through payroll and the questions of dividend and holding structure; and the transition from eenmanszaak to BV without losing the personal bookkeeper.
outcomes: VOF partners see one administration and a correct profit split, and every partner's income tax return is filed from the same figures
BV clients have their corporate tax return filed, statutory accounts deposited at KVK and DGA payroll run at a fixed fee
A freelancer who grows into a BV moves to Founders on the same platform with the history intact

flows.trigger: The fourth quarter of the VOF is filed and the year-end season opens for partnerships.
flows.successSignal: The VOF annual accounts show the profit split and capital accounts per partner, and every partner's income tax return is filed with the entrepreneur deductions applied where the hours criterion is met.

steps.title: Close the shared administration
keyFacts: The VOF's ledger is closed like a sole proprietor's, with private withdrawals and deposits per partner tracked on capital accounts during the year.
Both partners' submissions are in one administration so the close is one job.
painPoints: Withdrawals not tagged to a partner make the capital accounts unreliable.
Partners who mix their private accounts with the VOF account create reconciliation work.

flows.title: Move from Eenmanszaak to BV and Run the BV Year
flows.description: A knowledge freelancer whose profit outgrows the sole proprietorship sets up a holding and a werkmaatschappij with Founders: the transition is planned, the BV administration starts on the same platform, DGA salary is run through payroll and the first BV year ends with a corporate tax return, statutory accounts and the KVK filing.

keyFacts: The knowledge base guides the comparison: income tax with deductions versus corporate tax plus DGA salary and dividend, liability, the timing of incorporation and the fiscal options for transferring the business.
The advice is given by the bookkeeper with a Founders colleague where needed, without hourly fees.
painPoints: Freelancers incorporate on the advice of a peer without checking whether the profit level justifies it.
Advice given without documenting the assumptions cannot be revisited when the profit changes.

streams.name: Ask Your Bookkeeper and Get Advice
streams.description: Make the personal bookkeeper the client's fiscal home: questions by e-mail and phone, video or in-person meetings on request at the Amsterdam, Rotterdam or Utrecht office, answers that are consistent across some forty bookkeepers in three offices because they draw on the advice knowledge base (deductions, mkb-winstvrijstelling, KOR, hours criterion, buying a house as a freelancer, entrepreneurship next to a job, Wet DBA, pensions, the BV question), proactive updates on deadlines and rule changes, and a backup colleague when the bookkeeper is away, all within the fixed fee.
outcomes: Clients get a correct, consistent answer within a working day or two, without an hourly fee and without repeating their story
Advice on big decisions (house, BV, pension, Wet DBA) is documented on the file and backed by the knowledge base
Clients hear about a rule change or deadline from Kees before they read about it elsewhere

flows.title: Answer a Client Question with the Knowledge Base
flows.description: A creative freelancer asks whether a course, a studio and a new laptop are deductible and how the Wet DBA affects a long assignment; the question is routed, answered from the knowledge base, logged and, where new, fed back into the base.
flows.trigger: The client sends a question by e-mail, from the app, or calls the bookkeeper.
flows.successSignal: The client has a documented answer on the file, the bookkeeper spent minutes not an hour, and any new question pattern is added to the knowledge base.

steps.title: Ask the question from the app, by e-mail or by phone
keyFacts: Questions can be attached to a booking, an invoice or a dashboard figure so the context travels with them; phone calls are logged by the bookkeeper with the same context.
The client sees the expected response time.
painPoints: Questions without context ('is this deductible?') need a round trip.
Calls not logged leave the backup colleague without history.

dependencies.name: Client Messaging, E-mail and Call Log

dependencies.name: Mobile App Shell (iOS/Android)

keyFacts: The question lands on the personal bookkeeper's queue; if the bookkeeper is on leave or overloaded, the backup colleague in the same office takes it with the client file at hand.
Response times are tracked per bookkeeper and office.
painPoints: Questions waiting in a personal mailbox during a holiday are the most common complaint.
Backups who do not know the client's history give generic answers.

Standard answers keep forty bookkeepers in three offices consistent; tailoring keeps them personal.

Rules that changed this year but not in the base produce confident wrong answers.

painPoints: Advice given by phone and not logged is disputed at year end.
Answers without a follow-up to-do are forgotten by the client.

painPoints: Big decisions handled in an e-mail thread miss the client's real situation.
Meetings without a logged outcome are repeated a year later.

flows.title: Proactively Update Clients on Rule Changes and Deadlines

steps.title: Track the change and update the knowledge base

rootGroups.name: Growth and Operations Journeys
rootGroups.description: From partner agreements and satisfied clients to referred members and ambassadors, and from client volume per office to allocated bookkeepers, four-eyes checks and internal training: the journeys that grow the brand toward 20,000 clients and run the human layer as a product.

streams.name: Grow Through Partners and Referrals
streams.description: Turn professional associations, insurers, pension and legal providers (BNO, DuPho, Kunstenbond, Stichting BOK with 2,300+ members, voordekunst, Unfair, Insify, BrightPensioen with a €50 discount, DAS) into member benefits and referral channels, and turn satisfied clients into ambassadors through client stories, video testimonials, entrepreneur network profiles and the blog. Referral codes and partner pages attribute every intro call to its source, so growth toward 20,000 clients is data-driven rather than word of mouth alone.
outcomes: Every partner has a live member benefit, a tracked referral link and a quarterly view of referred members activated
Referred freelancers convert from intro call to active client at a higher rate than cold leads because the partner's trust carries over
Client stories and network profiles are published with consent and feed the acquisition funnel for the creative and starter segments

flows.title: Launch a Partner Benefit and Track Referrals
flows.description: A professional association agrees a member benefit with Kees: the benefit is defined (for example no administration costs and three months free, or a discount), the partner page and referral code go live, referred members are attributed through the intro call and onboarding, and the partner receives a report.
flows.trigger: A professional association, insurer or service provider agrees a partnership, or an existing partner renews and wants a new benefit.
flows.successSignal: The benefit is live on the partner's member pages and the Kees partner page, referred members are attributed from request to active client, and the partner has received the first uptake report.

steps.title: Define the member benefit and the partner agreement
keyFacts: The benefit is defined per partner (for example Stichting BOK members: no administration costs and three months free; BrightPensioen: a €50 discount), with its validity, eligibility (proof of membership) and how it is applied to the subscription.
Reciprocal benefits for Kees clients (insurance, pension, legal help through the partner) are recorded on the same agreement.
painPoints: Benefits that are not expressible as a subscription rule are applied by hand and inconsistently.
Partners expect exclusivity or volume promises that the fixed-fee model cannot give.

Pages that do not state the benefit in one sentence are not read by members.

streams.name: Plan Bookkeeper Capacity and Quality
streams.description: Run the human layer of the service as a product: forecast client volume per office (Amsterdam, Rotterdam, Utrecht) and season, allocate clients to internally trained bookkeepers with balanced portfolios and named backups, plan the quarterly VAT and income tax peaks, run risk-based four-eyes checks and sampling, measure review turnaround and first-time-right per bookkeeper, and feed the findings into internal training. With roughly 40 percent of ~100 staff being bookkeepers, clients served per bookkeeper is the number that decides whether 20,000 clients is reachable at the same fixed fee.
outcomes: Every bookkeeper carries a portfolio sized to their experience and the season, with a named backup, so no client waits because of a holiday or a departure
Quality is measured (first-time-right, corrections, review turnaround) per bookkeeper and office and drives training, not blame
Capacity for the next quarter and the income tax season is planned from client growth per office before the peak, not during it

flows.title: Plan the Quarter's Capacity per Office
flows.description: Before the quarter close and the income tax season, operations forecasts the workload from client counts and complexity per office, balances portfolios, assigns backups, plans training and hiring and sets the review priorities.
flows.trigger: The next quarter close or the income tax season approaches, or client growth in an office outpaces its bookkeepers.
flows.successSignal: Every client is allocated to a bookkeeper with capacity and a backup, the peak plan per office is agreed and the review priorities are loaded into the queues.

steps.title: Forecast the workload from client counts and complexity
keyFacts: The forecast counts active clients per office by legal form, add-ons (payroll, bank connection), switch cases and starters, weights them by expected review time and adds the season's income tax returns.
Historical review times per client type calibrate the weights.
painPoints: Counting clients without complexity treats a VOF with payroll as a starter with ten receipts.
Forecasts made after onboarding surges are too late to hire.

dependencies.name: Client Allocation and Workload Planning
dependencies.how: Computes the weighted workload per office and season.

dependencies.name: Onboarding, Fit Check and Bookkeeper Matching
dependencies.how: Provides expected new clients from the onboarding pipeline.

steps.title: Balance portfolios and assign backups
keyFacts: Portfolios are balanced by weighted workload and experience; each bookkeeper has a named backup in the same office, and clients are moved only when necessary and with a personal introduction.
New bookkeepers start with smaller portfolios of simpler clients.
painPoints: Moving clients between bookkeepers for balance breaks the personal relationship that is the product.
Backups assigned on paper without capacity cannot actually cover.

dependencies.name: Client Allocation and Workload Planning
dependencies.how: Proposes allocations and backups and records them.

dependencies.name: Bookkeeper Client File and Review Queue
dependencies.how: Updates the assigned bookkeeper and backup on each client file.

dependencies.name: Client Messaging, E-mail and Call Log

steps.title: Plan the peak and the deadline schedule
keyFacts: The filing calendar spreads the quarter's returns across the month after the quarter and the income tax returns across the season, with early-completeness clients first and known late clients chased earlier.
Leave is planned around the peaks and backups are confirmed for the peak weeks.
painPoints: Everyone filing in the last week of the month makes the tax authority channel the bottleneck.
Peaks planned without leave data leave offices short in the holiday season.

dependencies.name: Filing Calendar and Deadline Orchestration

dependencies.name: Client Allocation and Workload Planning

Rules are adjusted from last period's quality findings.
painPoints: Rules that never change do not respond to new error patterns.
Sampling rates set too high during the peak are silently abandoned.

Training topics come from the quality findings of the last period.
painPoints: Hiring after the peak has started means training during the peak.
Training built on generic accounting skills misses the Kees way of working.

keyFacts: Team leads in Amsterdam, Rotterdam and Utrecht review the plan, confirm allocations and backups and flag clients that need special attention.
The confirmed plan is recorded and the queues are opened.
painPoints: Plans made centrally without the team leads ignore what they know about their clients.
Unconfirmed plans lead to two people working the same file.

flows.title: Measure Quality and Close the Training Loop
flows.description: After a filing period, the quality team measures first-time-right, corrections, review turnaround and client feedback per bookkeeper and office, reviews findings with the bookkeepers, updates the knowledge base and adjusts the rules for the next period.
flows.trigger: A filing period (a quarterly VAT cycle or the income tax season) is complete.
flows.successSignal: Quality metrics per bookkeeper and office are reviewed, root causes are addressed in training and the knowledge base, and the next period's rules and allocations reflect the findings.

steps.title: Collect the quality signals of the period
keyFacts: Four-eyes findings, supplementary returns and their coded causes, Belastingdienst correction letters, review turnaround per client and client feedback are collected per bookkeeper and office.
Signals are linked to the file and the bookkeeper who handled it.
painPoints: Findings recorded in e-mails and spreadsheets cannot be aggregated.

keyFacts: The team lead reviews the findings with each bookkeeper: patterns (VAT codes, private use, investments), client-related causes and workload effects; actions are agreed and recorded.
Reviews are development conversations, not disciplinary ones.
painPoints: Findings delivered as a list without the files behind them are not accepted.
Reviews skipped during the peak lose the learning while it is fresh.

keyFacts: Recurring findings become training modules and knowledge base articles; standard answers and booking rules are adjusted so the error is prevented rather than caught.
The app's to-do rules can be changed to catch the client-side causes.
painPoints: Training that does not change a rule or an article has to be repeated every period.
Client-side causes fixed by more review instead of better prompts do not scale.

keyFacts: Four-eyes rules and sampling rates are tuned to the error patterns found, and allocations are adjusted where a bookkeeper's portfolio or client mix drove the findings.

painPoints: Rules tightened after every finding make the second check universal and the bottleneck permanent.
Allocation changes without a rationale look arbitrary to bookkeepers.

painPoints: Reports without the link to automation candidates keep capacity a hiring problem only.
Leadership reports that arrive after the next period's plan is made are too late to matter.
